description: A simplified solderless breadboard with a plus rail, a minus rail, and numbered columns split by a center gap. Clicking a hole highlights every hole joined to it by the same internal strip. A battery, a jumper wire, a resistor, and an LED are already placed, with one connection missing. The Complete the Circuit button adds the final jumper, after which moving dots show conventional current flowing around the closed loop and the LED lights.

educational.topic: Internal connections of a solderless breadboard and current flow in a closed circuit
learningObjectives: Demonstrate which breadboard holes are electrically connected.
Demonstrate how current flows once a simple LED circuit is completed.
Identify the missing connection in an open circuit.
prerequisites: Knows that a battery has a positive and a negative terminal
Has read the definitions of solderless breadboard and breadboard tie points

controls.label: Breadboard hole
controls.description: Highlights every hole in the same tie point group: the whole rail, or the five holes of that column on one side of the center gap

controls.label: Complete the Circuit
controls.description: Adds the final jumper wire from hole j7 to the minus rail, closing the loop and starting the current animation

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Removes the final jumper wire and clears the highlight

simulation.modelType: Connectivity model of a breadboard with a single-loop circuit
equations: Two holes are connected when they are in the same rail, or in the same column on the same side of the center gap
Current flows only when the loop from battery plus to battery minus is closed
assumptions: One plus rail at the top and one minus rail at the bottom; each rail is continuous
Each numbered column has two groups of five holes, rows a to e and rows f to j
The dots show conventional current, from plus to minus
limitations: Real boards usually have a plus and minus rail pair on each long edge, and some split their rails at the middle
Voltages, resistance, and current are not calculated; the LED is either dark or lit

pedagogical.pattern: Direct manipulation followed by an observed consequence
pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner probes holes to discover the connection rule, finds the open point in the circuit, then completes it and observes the result
keyQuestions: Which holes share a strip with the one you clicked?
Where does the path from battery plus stop before the circuit is completed?
commonMisconceptions: Holes that are next to each other are connected
The two halves of a column are connected across the center gap
Current flows as soon as a battery is attached, even if the loop is open
assessmentOpportunities: Predict whether two named holes are connected, then check by clicking
Name the missing connection before completing the circuit
